subject: Spec review done: verdict FAIL, 8 blocking
body: Verdict FAIL: I ran /sc:spec-panel-armb in critique mode (requirements and architecture) on orca-worker-contract-spec.md, re-checked its load-bearing citations against the files, and wrote the full panel result with a numbered findings list to review/spec-panel.md without editing the spec. The core decision (Orca coordinates, commands stay the units of work) holds, but there are 8 blocking findings: WC-4 status values clash with the existing success value (F1); contract paths are undefined for file-output and workflow commands (F2); the Phase 0 and Phase 1 checks cannot pass as written (F3, F4); a retry overwrites the first attempt (F5); WC-10 conflicts with Agent-tool fan-out (F6); cli-portify gates have no answer flag (F7); and WC-7 never says the skill must be loaded (F8). Left for Task 6: revise the spec for F1-F8 per the Reviser brief in the report; 8 minor notes are optional, and no live Orca run or test run was made.

subject: Spec revised: 8 blocking findings applied, 16 dispositions
body: I checked all 16 findings in review/spec-panel.md (F1-F8 blocking, N1-N8 notes) against the cited lines; all held, and I applied F1-F8 to specs/orca-worker-contract-spec.md: a full status mapping (F1), a worker-owned run folder <base>/<dispatch_id>/ that fixes both the contract path and retry overwrites (F2, F5; workflow is a named exception), Phase 0 pass conditions (F3), the --unattended section arriving only in each command's conversion phase (F4), an Agent-tool exemption from the 4-minute rule (F6), named answer inputs for blocked gates (F7), and a required Skill-tool call (F8). Notes N2-N8 and half of N1 were applied; the other half of N1 (one shared rule for remediation offers) was rejected with cited reasons, and the spec grew from 57,763 to 65,568 bytes with no placeholder left. Still open: three new UNVERIFIED items (spec items 15-17: dispatch ID in the worker-start receipt, tdd/init-lite parent folders, Skill-tool reachability), no live run, and the revised spec needs review 2 of 3.

subject: Round-2 spec review: FAIL, 7 blocking open
body: I re-reviewed the revised spec independently: checked all 16 round-1 findings against the live spec text, re-read 25 citations the revision added or changed, and ran /sc:spec-panel-armb (critique, requirements and architecture) in re-review mode as review 2 of 3. Six of the eight round-1 blocking findings are resolved; F1 stays open because adversarial nests its status under return_contract, so WC-5 reports a successful run as failed and the step-4 check raises KeyError, and F3 stays open because the adversarial Phase 0 smoke run has no expected report path. Five new blocking findings were introduced or exposed by the revision: cli-portify's dry_run is unmapped, the universal contract path contradicts 8 section-3 rows, an unattended implement overwrites the workflow package's contract and breaks the D2(a) resume, WC-3's new no-ask rule contradicts D2(b) and pr-submit, and AC-1.2 passes --output to workflow and init-lite. Citations: 2 wrong line or step numbers, both minor. Verdict FAIL; one fix cycle remains before escalation, and the Reviser brief is in the report.

subject: Round-2 findings applied to spec
body: Checked all 15 round-2 findings (NF1-NF7, M1-M8) and the two flagged citations (C8, C11) against the source files and applied every one; none was rejected, and each has a row in review/disposition-round2.md giving the spec line it changed. Three root causes were fixed once rather than patched per row: every command except workflow now writes its contract in its own per-dispatch run folder, received through its folder output flag, a file output path, or a new --run-dir flag (NF3, NF4, NF6, NF7); the outcome check reads adversarial's nested return_contract block and accepts dry_run (NF1, NF2); and the pr-submit row and decision D2 (b) no longer use ask, which matches WC-3 (NF5). The spec grew from 65,568 to 70,579 bytes, its placeholder scan is clean, no tracked file changed, and what remains is review 3 of 3 plus two new open questions (does every quick adversarial run write merge-log.md, and is the --run-dir name free).

subject: fix audit applied(reverted=1, shrunk=1, kept=12)
body: Ran /sc:spec-panel-ponytail --fix-audit once through the sc-fix-audit script (prepare, ponytail-review audit, check CHECK_OK, apply); the spec was edited only by the script, and the pre-audit copy is at review/fix-audit/current-before-audit.md. Result is audit: applied(reverted=1, shrunk=1, kept=12): the M3 hunk H8 was reverted to the baseline and the unattributed WC-10 citation split (H2) was trimmed, while every blocking fix (NF1-NF7) stays in place; three more shrink edits I proposed (a repeated NF1 sentence in WC-5 and 7.2 step 4, and UNVERIFIED item 19 about the --run-dir name) were skipped by the script because another row keeps the same hunk. Left for the coordinator: run review 3, then the skill's verdict step on the review-3 report (review 3 must not read fix-audit/audit.md); closed-minor.txt lists M3.

subject: Review 3 complete: minor-only FAIL
body: I completed review 3 and wrote the resolution, citation-check and boundary tables without editing the spec. All seven prior blocking findings are resolved and no new findings were verified, but the final verdict is FAIL under the assigned any-severity rule because the optional brief-template note remains open. The coordinator should reconcile the disposition with that intentional revert and report the minor-only outcome, with no fourth review or implementation run.
